Peter Willis — we’re in an
existential fight for our country.

On one side, Trump, Musk and the billionaire class want to privatize the
government and plunder our tax dollars to pad their pockets. Through
de-regulation, de-unionization, and slashing taxes for the rich, they
aren’t shy about their plans to destroy public education, Social Security,
Medicare, and much more. All so they can profit even more.

On the other side is Bernie and our movement. Bernie just said that
Oligarchy is THE most important issue facing our country and our fight for
a progressive future. [ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/20829?t=1061&akid=7455%2E5885482%2EKYD1nN ]Can you chip in right now to help Bernie & Our
Revolution organize to stop the privatization of critical public goods by
Trump, Musk, and the Oligarchs?

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/20829?t=1062&akid=7455%2E5885482%2EKYD1nN ][IMG]

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/20829?t=1063&akid=7455%2E5885482%2EKYD1nN ][IMG]

Privatization means taking popular public programs and jacking up costs to
produce a profit for billionaires. Musk is already $200 billion richer
after just this past year when he spent $277 million backing Trump and
other far right candidates. Big Tech monopolies like Zuckerberg’s Facebook
and Bezos’ Amazon are jumping on board to kiss the ring and pour big money
into Trump’s inauguration fund.

The ultra-wealthy are coalescing around the Trump admin and preparing to
profit from policies that will harm working-class people. Bernie is
calling on us to take on the Oligarchs, and the only way we can do it is
with the resources to mount massive campaigns to hold the line.

Oligarchs and billionaire class? We need to take up Bernie's rallying call
and stop Trump-Musk from their privatize and plunder agenda.

If you've stored your payment information with ActBlue Express, your
donation to Our Revolution will process immediately.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/20725?t=1047?express_lane=true&amount=66&refcode=email-20241231nd&akid=7455%2E5885482%2EKYD1nN ]CHIP IN $66 [ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/20725?t=1048?&amount=9&refcode=email-20241231nd&akid=7455%2E5885482%2EKYD1nN ]CHIP IN OTHER AMOUNT

The Musk-Trump agenda will impact all of us. It will touch every part of
society. Just one example: Housing.

Trump wants to privatize Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, which would jack up
mortgage payments — hurting homeowners while allowing private operators to
get even richer. This is an outright assault on the American Dream.

We’re already in a housing crisis — with a supply shortage, mortgage rates
high, home prices up, and Wall Street jacking up rent prices. The
privatize and plunder agenda would make things even worse, except for the
billionaire class, of course.

Banks already make plenty of money off of mortgages. Private equity
already makes outrageous profits from buying up whole neighborhoods and
inflating rent prices. This is all part of the cost of living crisis —
which Trump and his cronies are lining up to exploit even more.

Bernie and Our Revolution won’t just let Trump-Musk get away with this.
There’s too much on the line, and we need a mass movement at our back,
speaking out and exposing their plan to plunder the American people.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/20725?t=1054?express_lane=true&amount=22&refcode=email-20241231nd&akid=7455%2E5885482%2EKYD1nN ]Donate now to make sure we have the resources to fight the Trump-Musk
privatize and plunder agenda. We gotta start NOW before Trump takes office
Jan 20th.

name: Jocelyn Benson
subject: A quick 2024 Recap
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY JOCELYN BENSON FOR SECRETARY OF STATE
body:
# [](https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/5?t=1&akid=18%2E181023%2E0KNHpQ)
I’m closing out 2024 with gratitude. This was such an important year for our state, and while we reflect, I want to share the top 10 moments I’m most grateful for. I hope you’ll stick around -- this email is a longer one!
#10: I’m so grateful for the election workers and clerks across our state who worked tirelessly to deliver safe and secure elections, especially the November election which saw Michigan's highest-ever turnout: 5.7 million votes cast. This was truly a team effort — and we could not have done it without everyone’s dedication and grit.
#9: This year's historic turnout was made possible by the adoption of statewide early in-person voting via a 2022 ballot measure. I am grateful to the people of Michigan for recognizing the importance of expanding access to the ballot box.
#8: Working with Governor Gretchen Whitmer and Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel every day was a huge blessing. I’m so grateful for their continued partnership, friends, and support. We’re really working hard to deliver for the people of Michigan.
#7: Being a woman from Michigan is a badge of honor. I'm grateful to the voters of our state for continuing to elect strong, powerful women warriors in 2024 including Elissa Slotkin, Hillary Scholten, Haley Stevens, Debbie Dingell, Rashida Tlaib, Kristen McDonald Rivet, Kyra Harris Bolden, Kimberly Ann Thomas, and many more!
#6: The power of the people will always be greater than the people in power. That's why I am always grateful for leaders and members of Michigan's unions. They fight tirelessly every day to ensure everyone is safe and valued in their workplace.
#5: The Lions. #OnePride
#4: I am so grateful for the team working at the Michigan Department of State. Everyone is dedicated to delivering excellent government and defending democracy, and that dedication will continue in 2025.
#3 The local leaders, lawmakers, and other public servants who dedicated this year to fighting tirelessly on behalf of their communities. Their dedication ensures our government is more transparent, ethical, and efficient.
#2: Serving Michigan as your Secretary of State has been one of the greatest honors of my life. I am grateful every day to wake up and get to work on saving people time and money and increasing engagement in our democracy.
#1: My favorite job of all is being a mom. Grateful to have such an awesome kid who drives my passion for making sure Michigan is a place where anyone can be a kid and raise a kid.
Thank you for your support throughout the year. Without you, we could not have accomplished all the great things for our state.
Let’s keep on the fight,
Jocelyn

* * *

Before you go... we need your help. Since her 2018 election, Secretary Benson has fought for free and fair elections. She’s on the front lines of defending and strengthening our democracy. **[Will you contribute today to show your support?](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jb-em-20241231-1?refcode=em20241231-1&refcode2=18_181023_0KNHpQ&akid=18%2E181023%2E0KNHpQ)** **[Donate »](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jb-em-20241231-1?refcode=em20241231-1&refcode2=18_181023_0KNHpQ&akid=18%2E181023%2E0KNHpQ)**

It's Gretchen Whitmer.

2024 has been one hell of a year. This election cycle showed us an America deeply divided over our vision for this country, and as a result of that division, many of our fundamental freedoms are sure to come under threat in new and outrageous ways.

In times of upheaval, we need to look to what has always been true. And here's what I know for sure: More freedom is better than less. Some rights, like the right to make our own medical decisions, are nonnegotiable. And when more women are at the decision-making table, we all win.

Friend, it’s Lieutenant Governor Aruna Miller. During this time of giving, I want to take a moment to thank you for your support. It’s people like you who fuel the movement to make this Maryland’s decade, and for that, we’re eternally grateful. Wes and I have been able to pass**26 out of the 26 bills** we introduced during the last two legislative sessions. They have strengthened our economy, health care, and more issues that matter to Marylanders. But the fight isn’t over yet. subject: *RESULTS* - NEGOP Truth in Taxation Poll
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY THE NEBRASKA REPUBLICAN PARTY]( "PAID FOR BY THE NEBRASKA REPUBLICAN PARTY")
body:
HIGH Property Taxes are HURTING Nebraskans! | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/31f0ae09b732/n41kepo7ku-12725552?e=25844e23a8)
---
| | [ ](https://gop.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=1d82dcd2e67c4075340c26b37&id=7fb069e296&e=25844e23a8)
---
| | Peter, Chairman Underwood here.

Thank you to all who participated in the NEGOP Priority Poll on _**Truth in Taxation**_. As promised, I wanted to reach out to you FIRST with the results. Almost **450 responses** came in and provided a CLEAR picture of what is YOUR taxation priorities. Property taxes are impacting Nebraskans and we have to BOLD and make a change sooner rather than later.
* Almost all have education beyond High school, whether OTJ, Military, or College
* Experienced in life
* They HAVE to reduce their family spending.
* Almost 3/5's are or have considered leaving Nebraska!
* They are about half rural and half urban — by far the largest segment being urban home-owners.
* About 84% want reduced property tax levies.
* 84% are willing to raise sales tax rates IF, and ONLY IF, tax revenue INCREASE was necessary AFTER prioritizing REDUCING GOVERNMENT SPENDING.

The party will study demographic responses soonest and present information to other party leaders. The NEGOP will work with our Unicameral Senators to make sure your VOICE is heard.

---
| | NEBRASKA'S VOICES

_Most noticeable to me is the increase in everyday items. I rent, and my landlord has been quite benevolent in not raising rent much. The price of groceries and gas has increased in the last few years, but I know for sure the gas price is artificially increased. My nephew is a CPA and works for a large Midwest convenience store corporation. He said they're just raising the gas prices to see how much people will pay, and that the gas segment of the convenience store has, by far, been more profitable in the last 4 years than the in-store sales. Normally, in-store sales are the profit generator. It's all just a game of corporate greed. _

\--Fremont, Ne

_Increase housing which increased insurance. The value of a county going up should reduce the millevy but it just give the county more money to spend._

\--Hastings, Ne

_Our retirement income is based on the rental money we get from the 3 small (4 units each) apartments we own._

\--Norfolk, Ne

_Goods and supplies. My home is not very expensive, so taxes are not to terrible. But the cost of medical services and Insurance is through the roof ridiculous. But Insurance is ridiculous!_

\--Oakland, Ne

_Spending is out of control. If I ran my family budget like the federal, state and county does the law would be after me. I am a disabled veteran and it is becoming more difficult to maintain._

\--Dakota City, Ne

_As a retired person with a paid off mortgage, my largest annual expense is property tax. I can control my spending on other goods but I can’t change my property tax. This tax is a threat to continued homeownership for Seniors._

\--Kearney, Ne

_Property taxes on a new house are very high. Recent reductions in income tax have been beneficial in exempting military retirement pay and federal employee retirement._

\--Papillion, Ne

_Housing costs and other real estate taxes. Way out of control. Need to eliminate Real Estate taxes with EPIC option!_

\--Scottsbluff, Ne

_My farm in Jefferson county is nearly 10k annually for less than 160 acres. I don’t know how the farmers can make it! Our politicians don’t seem to have a plan except to spend and are beholden to education. I’ve reached out but minimal response back! Or the response is..’ you’re not in my district’ or ‘ that’s the way it is’_

\--Lincoln, Ne

_Buying groceries for my family of 6 has been difficult in just the last 2 years. I can’t leave the store without spending at least $200 on things that won’t even last me a week. Property taxes have become so high we have considered moving to another state to get some relief. Home owner’s insurance is another story too. We are almost where we can’t afford our monthly payment between property taxes and insurance increases._

\--Omaha, Ne

Jimmy Carter, our 39th president, passed away at the age of 100. He was the oldest living US President.
[Pledge your support](https://substack..0zzQs6avnByr13zLcH5H_DMkrhRB41nZxHLG5hFPOOI?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=153858525)
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=1454853&post_id=153858525&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTUzODU4NTI1LCJpYXQiOjE3MzU2NzAxNzMsImV4cCI6MTczODI2MjE3MywiaXNzIjoicHViLTE0NTQ4NTMiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.dLKdWTLD31hcBx0DOjN4mFxmoqIo-iuDNiAhge7vCdU)
Jimmy Carter's presidency and his legacy have had a profound impact on the American tapestry that we call our American history. President Carter was a one-term President who won the nomination as an outsider for the '76 presidential election. He rose from a no-name peanut farmer, school teacher and "outsider" (even though he was a Governor) to President in less than 2 years.
Thanks for reading Michael's Substack! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work.
[Pledge your support](https://substack..0zzQs6avnByr13zLcH5H_DMkrhRB41nZxHLG5hFPOOI?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=153858525)
His presidency was not one of the better times of our nation and marked an era of true American Failures.
_**Those who lived through it faced rampant inflation, high interest rates, energy shortages, and a challenging diplomatic and foreign relations to say the least. Americans waited on line to buy gas with horrible shortages.**_
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/18a53d13-c43a-4ee9-90a8-3070a36f6e8a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/3e0e78b1-81bd-4b77-80fb-3e22e47ce622?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_**Home mortgage rates rose above 14 percent which are more than double what they are today and these rates now are considered unaffordable.**_
**Iran**
_**Carter 's lack of support for the Shah of Iran and his administration's secret talks with Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini resulted in the overthrow of the Shah. Khomeini was the architect of the Iranian Revolution and installed himself as the first leader of the Islamic republic in 1979.**_
This revolution resulted in the taking of the American Embassy in Tehran by Iranian students loyal to Khomeini from November 4, 1979 to their release on January 20, 1981.
Most notably, President Carter was credited with the poor rescue of Americans held in the Iranian embassy that led the accidental death of eight servicemen. Those hostages were released 444 days later on January 20, 1981, the day that Ronald Reagan took office. **It is likely that the hostages were released as Khomeini perceived Reagan to be a credible threat.**
It was those political challenges of Carter's administration that likely paved the way for the Reagan era. Carter's blunders galvanized a nation and Reagan even won 40% of the Jewish votes setting the high-water mark for the GOP despite Carter's role in the Camp David Accords.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu remembered "President Carter's crucial role in facilitating the first Arab-Israeli peace treaty."
President-elect Trump stated "The challenges Jimmy faced as President came at a pivotal time for our country and he did everything in his power to improve the lives of all Americans. For that, we all owe him a debt of gratitude."
**Carter Faced Challenges**
Carter also lead the charge to boycott the 1980 Olympics in Moscow and took other steps in strengthening the nation against Russia which he is not always credited for.
Carter is also remembered for his Cold War military strategy that he unveiled as part of his 1980 State of the Union which stated that the Soviets' Afghanistan invasion and attempts to takeover that region was a threat to the US. At the time, Carter supported Mujahideen guerilla's in Afghanistan following the Soviet invasion. At the time, President Carter realized that military force was necessary. At that same State of the Union addressed, Carter pledged to begin a five-year spending initiative to modernize and strengthen the military because Carter realized that the US was ill-prepared in a post-Vietnam that was plagued by military.
President Reagan likely rose to popularity due to the continued big-red scare of the Soviets coupled with the political instability and military challenges attributed to Carter along with a horrible economy. However, Reagan did acknowledge Carter's foresight years later and praised the former President's record on military preparedness.
Carter's foreign policy in Latin America did leave an impression that led thousands of Cuban, Haitian and Nicaraguan refugees to flee their war-torn dictatorships to the United States while the US struggled to promote democracy. Carter also signed the Refugee Act of 1980 placing a "humanitarian" focus and changed the definition of "refugee" to a person with a "well-founded fear of persecution" according to standards established by United Nations conventions and protocols.
**A Love for Music and the First to Galvanize the Youth**
Carter's election was probably the first one to raise significant funds through popular recording artists. Jimmy Carter credited his victory to the Allman Brothers. In 2016, as he gave Gregg Allman an honorary degree at Mercer University in Macon, Georgia, Carter stated that "Gregg Allman and the Allman Brothers just about put me in the White House," The legislation changed to allow for matching dollars and The Allman Brothers were "were the best fundraisers that we had. In those days, they would charge somebody $15 to come hear them play. And we were getting the whole $15 plus 15 more matching dollars! So we got $30 every time someone came to hear the Allman Brothers Band play."
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/56fb4cb9-5c3f-4c34-aaf6-c8d32336c77b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
This unique team of Carter and the Allman Brothers helped bring in the youth vote coming off Woodstock. It has led to decades where the popularity of a recording artist help to raise funds or awareness for politicians. _**This trend did not work for the most recent Presidential election despite heavy influence of Hollywood actors and notable recording artists cheerleading for Kamala Harris.**_
**Humanitarian Off the Field (or out of the White House)**
President Biden praised President Carter's decency and stated that he [Carter] "lived a life measured not by words, but by his deeds."
Since his presidency, President Carter was probably one of the most influential and successful presidents to use his diplomacy and relations to impact the community at large. President Carter did more as a civilian and to impact and better the lives of mostly Americans. He had a charitable heart and many benefited as a result. He will be best know for his ties to Habitat for Humanity. Through the Carter Work Project at Habitat for Humanity. Jimmy and his wife Rosalynn inspired more than 108,000 volunteers across the U.S. and in 14 countries to get involved, build, renovate and repair 4,447 Habitat homes.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/7fdb6450-4cef-4654-a854-4bdfe5bd3333?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
His influence and personal beliefs on Israel and the West Bank and his 2006 book, "[Palestine: Peace Not Apartheid](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/8a4b4cdf-0266-4f0f-bfce-757f597c5c58?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)," exacerbated Carter's "complicated" history and positions by comparing Israel's treatment of the Palestinians to South Africa's apartheid.
**Biden Era Parallels Carter Era**
What is interesting to note is the Carter era is very similar to the Biden era. The challenges that paved away for Ronald Reagan are similar ones that paved the way for president Donald Trump to win and be re-elected. Carter had inflation, fuel shortages, challenges with OPEC, and a very charged activist environment following Woodstock and Vietnam. There were also the challenges of the Soviet Union. In addition, Carter had the hostages that were Americans held in an embassy in Iran. Due to various political blunders in backing Khomeini and messaging, the US was perceived as weak under Carter and the US government was unable to leverage its power to have them released.
This is not unlike today and similar issues plague Americans, and the world at large. Russia invaded Ukraine and has been causing significant chaos and financial burdens to the United States along with the challenging humanitarian issues at play. The Hamas attack at the Nova festival and the hostages are still held today in Gaza are like the Iran hostage situation on a much larger scale.
As we know, Iran plays a critical role in the funding and shaping of Hamas's terrorist activities, and the Biden administration has been responsible for releasing funds that likely extended whatever leverage that Hamas has at the present moment.
**Final Thoughts**
President Carter was really a unique president. He was the only U.S. president to have taught Sunday school while in office but fully understood the separation between church and state.
It's not just what you do as a President. It's what you do after. Carter was the recipient of the Nobel peace prize for his extensive efforts in Middle East peace.
President Carter has left us many lessons that we can learn from, both positive and negative, and his lasting impact on improving the lives of Americans and those around the world in need.
He will also be known for challenging positions on the Middle East after his Presidency, a rocky relation with Israel and the West Bank. _He will also be remembered as the man that also gave up the Panama Canal which has now become at issue again._
As they say, those who fail to learn history are condemned to repeat it. Unfortunately, the memories have faded and America is just as susceptible to repeating its mistakes like any other political dynasty.
_**It is our responsibility as Americans to take care of those at home and help our neighbors and President Carter will be remembered for such humanitarian assistance.**_
A grateful nation mourns its former leader and his death is a good time for us to go back over the past few decades and really audit the pros and cons of all of our previous administrations. It is not a time for revisionist history which has plagued most obituaries on any former leader.
**Thank you for your continued support. Please subscribe and spread the word.**
Dr. Michael Goldstein & Jonathan Goldstein

Every battle we've taken on together – from enshrining protections for reproductive rights in New York to holding ultrawealthy and bad actors accountable – has been powered by your remarkable belief in justice and your unwavering commitment to our shared values.
Your support has given me the strength to keep going, no matter who has been standing in the way of our mission to protect and defend the hardworking families of New York.
So as we close out 2024, I want to leave you with this note before we head into the new year.
_**Thank you**_ for helping me ensure New York remains a safe haven for reproductive freedom.

**_Thank you_** for helping me fight for our nation's most vulnerable communities.

And **_thank you_** for standing by me in my pursuit of justice for all.
Every step forward, every hard-fought win, and every stand we've taken is because of incredible, fearless fighters like you, Peter.
**Together, we've built a legacy of progress and shown that no matter the odds, we can cultivate a country that works for _all_ of us. # _**Your YDA December Newsletter**_
---
_**Special Early New Year’s Message from Young Democrats of America President Quentin Wathum-Ocama**_
---
Dear Young Democrats and Supporters —

2024 was a tough year, and we need to be honest about that. We fought hard, poured our hearts into campaigns, and stood for the values we hold dear, but the results didn’t go our way. It’s a moment that has left many of us reflecting deeply on where we’ve been and what comes next.
Even in the face of disappointment, I see reasons for hope. I see it in the dedication of YDA members who continue to show up, even when the road is steep. I see it in the connections we’ve built and the movements we’ve nurtured—not just for one election cycle but for the long haul. Because that’s what this work is about: creating a better future, step by step, no matter how long it takes.

As we step into 2025, let’s embrace our unwavering purpose. We must stand resolutely against Republican policies that threaten our progress and the well-being of the most vulnerable. Simultaneously, we must not forsake marginalized communities in the pursuit of an elusive moderate. Our party's strength lies in our commitment to justice and inclusion, and we will steadfastly uphold those values.

**I believe in the power of young people to change the world. We’ve done it before, and we’ll do it again. Let’s work together this year to rebuild, reimagine, and reenergize.**
**In solidarity and hope,**
---
|
---
Quentin Wathum-Ocama
President, Young Democrats of America

# _**Winter Meeting Highlight: YDA National Committee Confirms Two New National Officers**_
---
|
---
At our Winter Meeting this past month in Boston, Massachusetts, the YDA National Committee voted to confirm 2 nonbinary young Democrats to our Executive Committee, Sam Jane (VA) will serve as YDA Treasurer and Katherine Jeanes (NC) as Democratic National Committee Representative.

Sam Jane is a seasoned fundraising and campaign professional with over a decade of experience at the local, state, and federal levels. A passionate reproductive justice advocate, Sam has dedicated their career to pro-choice causes, including running EMILY’s List’s national training program and founding Repro Workers to support abortion clinic staff and related initiatives.

Katherine Jeanes brings extensive experience, including serving on the DNC Youth Council and helping transform the Young Democrats of North Carolina into a leading force in organizing and fundraising.

# **_Winter Meeting Highlight: Young Democrats of America Host First Forum for DNC Chair Candidates_**
---
|
---
**Boston, MA** — _On December 7, the Young Democrats of America hosted the first forum for declared candidates for Chair of the Democratic National Convention in Boston, Massachusetts. The forum was candidates’ first and best opportunity to communicate directly with young people in the Democratic Party and make their case to Young Democrats from across the nation.

_ “It was an incredible honor to organize and hold the first forum for DNC Chair candidates. Each one of them talked about the importance of young people in their platforms and it’s refreshing that the candidates made a point to be here in Boston to spend time with YDA members. We may only have three votes on the DNC, but our members are the ones who are knocking doors, making calls, and doing the work to take back our country,” **said Stephanie Campanha Wheaton, the Young Democrats of America’s Senior Representative to the Democratic National Committee** “Each candidate voted to fully fund YDA and other youth organizations and we intend to hold the next Chair to this promise. We will not take back the White House, the House, or the Senate unless our youth organizers have the resources they need and deserve.”

“Investing in young people is no longer optional for Democrats. If the Democratic Party wants to start winning at the national level again, they need to make sure they’re investing in the young people who are doing the work to elect Democrats up and down the ballot, like we did in my home state of North Carolina,” **said Katherine Jeanes, the Young Democrats of America’s Junior Representative to the Democratic National Committee**. “I was pleased to hear every candidate for DNC Chair pledge to fully fund the Young Democrats because when leaders invest in young people, we make one hell of an impact."

“I’m very glad to have seen the candidates for DNC Chair at the Young Democrats’ meeting this weekend. I think our forum was a great success and an incredible opportunity for the candidates to make their pitch to the young people who make this party run,” **said Quentin Wathum-Ocama, President of the Young Democrats of America**. “When an organization like the DNC makes meaningful investments in young people, the returns are immeasurable. Our members know what they’re doing, and to have every declared candidate for DNC Chair pledge their support—in money and mentorship—means a lot."

_The candidates for DNC Chair are: Wisconsin Democratic Party Chair_**BEN WIKLER** _, Minnesota Democratic-Farmer-Labor Party Chair_**KEN MARTIN** _, New York State Senator_**JAMES SKOUFIS** _, and former Governor of Maryland_**MARTIN O’MALLEY** _.

WASHINGTON, DC — At the 1976 Democratic National Convention, President Carter made a promise to our nation that “the people run the government, not the other way around.” With unshakable integrity, he carried that promise through every stage in his life.
Today, Young Democrats across the nation join in mourning the loss of President Jimmy Carter—a proud son of Georgia, a Governor, a Naval Lieutenant, a peanut farmer, and a champion of civil rights. As President, he established the Department of Education, federally protected over 100 million acres of land and water, and brokered historic peace deals (including SALT II, the Camp David Accords, and the Panama Canal treaties).
President Carter's humility was perhaps his most remarkable trait. He treated every person he encountered— whether a world leader or a volunteer on a Habitat for Humanity build site— with the same respect, kindness, and dignity. He reminded us that the true measure of a person is not in the power they wield but in how they treat others once they've gained it. Today, it can be easy for us to feel disheartened by the future we face as a nation. Yet as President Carter once reminded us in his Inaugural Address: “We must adjust to changing times and still hold to unchanging principles.”
Now more than ever, we must uphold the unchanging principles of compassion, equality, and faith in humanity that guided Jimmy Carter throughout his life. Let them inspire us as we fight to expand voting rights, civil rights, access to healthcare, environmental protections, and reproductive rights. They remind us that, no matter how difficult the journey, progress is always worth pursuing.

Emphasizing affordable locations of note for meals and entertainment, alongside the walkability of the bid site is a plus; Ensure there are unionized hotels in the city, if there are none that is not a deal breaker however it does make a stronger bid; Propose hotels for your bid that are affordable for all members of our organization; Please be aware that typical National Committee meetings include 100 to 150 people. Please assume roughly half as many rooms will be required for the total number of attendees. Addressing the number of meeting rooms in your bid is a strength as well we request around 5 breakout style rooms and one large reception room; Quotes in advance always make a strong bid. Be sure to include A/V costs in your quotes. | | Hi Friend,
---
As we countdown the final hours of 2024, I know we’re all reflecting on the year that has passed.
---
And while we’ve been shaken, in the year ahead, we have the chance to lay down a marker for our values and articulate how we can achieve progress.
---
Today, as we make resolutions and set intentions for 2025, I wanted to share what I’m thinking about as I make my list.
---
I’m focused on ensuring that we continue to pursue economic opportunity for all, that we reject any attempts to limit power and prosperity to the few, and that we secure the freedoms and future that we deserve.
---
I would be grateful if you joined me again in that mission by helping us lay the foundation for the work to come by contributing to our efforts. It will help ensure we can be in as strong of a position as possible to kick off 2025.
---
[**DONATE**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/99608740/520415227/570291875?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDU0NTUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMWE0OWNiMjUtYThjNy1lZjExLTg4Y2UtMDAyMjQ4MmE5M2FmIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=MjdUfsMTY1aUEKgU7obuNiElehwf2THvpBwb_AaTdwI=)
---
Because of your support along this journey, I retain my optimism and commitment to a state, country, and world where we can all thrive. Make no mistake: it will be hard. So, let us continue to do this important work together.
---
Wishing you and your loved ones a happy, healthy, and harmonious New Year!
---
Let’s keep going,Gabe

body:
This year's top stories, plus Boebert’s Fish Recovery Act saves endangered fish, secures water for future generations
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
| | Happy New Year's Eve, friends!
As we prepare to ring in 2025, I want to take a moment to thank you for being with us during Rocky Mountain Voice’s very first year in business! Your support, engagement, and shared passion for truthful, community-driven journalism have been the foundation of everything we’ve achieved in 2024. We couldn’t have done it without you, and we’re excited to continue growing and serving Colorado in the year ahead.
Tonight, as you celebrate, please remember to be safe. Law enforcement across the state will have [increased DUI enforcement](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), so plan ahead if you’re drinking. Take advantage of [free RTD rides](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) and [discounted rideshare programs](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) to ensure you and your loved ones get home safely.
Looking for ways to celebrate? Colorado is buzzing with events, from [fireworks displays to light parades](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.).
Here's a summary of today's newsletter:
🎊 **Top Stories of 2024...** From election results that reshaped Colorado’s political landscape to high-profile controversies like password leaks, Tren de Aragua, and the visit of President Donald Trump, 2024 was a year of transformation. [Check out the top stories of 2024 here!](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
**🏔️ Here in Colorado...** Lauren Boebert’s [Fish Recovery Act](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) offers a bright spot, balancing conservation with securing vital water resources for agriculture and communities. Meanwhile, several [laws taking effect](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) in Colorado in 2025, while legislators are being urged to [focus on affordability](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) in the 75th session, with calls to reduce fees and regulations stifling economic growth. Additionally, debates continue over the[ role of elected sheriffs](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), with warnings against shifting to appointed positions that could undermine local accountability. Lastly, Jon Caldara offers a pragmatic take on [mass deportation policies](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), advocating for targeted enforcement over sweeping measures.
This is the Mountain Minute for Tuesday, December 31, 2024. Here’s to a joyful and prosperous 2025 for you and your family. Happy New Year, Colorado!
– Heidi Ganahl
---
|
---
**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[Top Stories of 2024: Elections, password leaks, Tren de Aragua, Trump visit and more](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY RMV STAFF, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
There’s one thing to say for 2024 in reflection — it wasn’t boring on the political front.
Along the way there were a dozen candidates for one highly coveted seat in the U.S. House, a once in three-decades special selection committee, a Secretary of State failing to keep passwords secure, the trial of Tina Peters, members of the GOP’s central committee unable to agree on leadership, a visit to the state from Donald J. Trump, gang violence in Aurora, Republican gains and much more.
Here’s a glance at some of the Colorado newsmakers and newsbreakers you may recall from 2024.
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**

---
**[Boebert’s Fish Recovery Act saves endangered fish, secures water for future generations](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* Lauren Boebert’s Fish Recovery Act, part of the FY 2025 National Defense Authorization Act, reauthorizes two critical programs until 2031 to protect four endangered fish species while supporting vital water and power infrastructure in Colorado.
* The act ensures the continuation of projects involving major reservoirs like Navajo and Flaming Gorge, supporting 3.7 million acre-feet of water use annually while promoting habitat restoration and species recovery.
* Backed by over 30 organizations, the bipartisan legislation benefits agriculture, municipal water users, and energy producers while preserving tribal water rights and advancing regional economic stability.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Lundberg: Get ready, there will be more laws for Colorado citizens in 2025](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* Several laws taking effect in Colorado in 2025 include stricter child restraint requirements, hands-free calling mandates for drivers, and new regulations for secure firearm storage in vehicles.
* Additional legislation includes measures requiring public schools to accommodate non-legal name changes, new excise taxes on firearms and ammunition, and stricter emissions standards targeting environmental justice.
* Critics argue these laws will increase living costs, limit personal freedoms, and burden local industries, sparking debates over their feasibility and long-term consequences.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Garbo: Sheriffs must always be elected to defend liberty and preserve the Constitution](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* The role of elected sheriffs is rooted in centuries-old traditions and the Colorado Constitution, ensuring local accountability and resistance to government overreach.
* Proposals to replace elected sheriffs with appointed officials threaten to centralize control, weaken accountability, and politicize law enforcement, contrasting sharply with the autonomy and constitutional focus of elected sheriffs.
* Highlighting the contrast between Denver’s politically appointed police leadership and the elected sheriff in Douglas County, the piece argues that elected sheriffs are essential for preserving public safety and individual freedoms.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Gonzalez: In the 75th legislative session, lawmakers should focus on affordability](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* Representative Ryan Gonzalez calls on Colorado lawmakers to prioritize reducing the cost of living by repealing unnecessary fees and scaling back regulations that increase everyday expenses for residents.
* Gonzalez advocates for an all-of-the-above energy approach, including oil and gas, to lower energy costs and support a strong sector, alongside reforms to housing codes to reduce burdensome costs on new developments.
* Emphasizing the role of private-public partnerships, Gonzalez urges the legislature to work with businesses to create meaningful solutions for housing, infrastructure, and transportation.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Caldara: Reality check on mass deportations in Colorado](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [COMPLETE COLORADO](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
_Let the meaningless battle over mass deportation in Colorado begin._
_Watching our cities virtue-signal on immigration is the best free entertainment your tax dollars can buy. The war of words and chest beating is worthy of a reality show._
_On one side, you have Denver’s Mayor Mike Johnston playing a modern-day Paul Revere. With those hideous Redcoats marching on Denver, his cry of “ICE is coming” will rally the Highland moms (who apparently cannot be messed with) and his own police force to take up arms to protect the immigrants who are bankrupting his city._
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|

**[Elected Republicans, from Denver to Washington, offered greetings on Christmas](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** **BY BRIAN PORTER | STATE | DECEMBER 26** _From the halls of Congress in Washington, D.C., to the Golden Dome in Denver, Republicans serving Colorado paused Wednesday not just to take time with family, but to turn to Twitter/X to communicate with constituents on the occasion of Christmas and the beginning of Hanukkah._
**[After six-year struggle, Boebert’s CONVEY Act now just needs Biden’s signature to transfer land to Mesa Co.](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)****BY JEN SCHUMANN****| STATE | DECEMBER 26** _Almost half of the land in the American West — 46.4% to be exact — is owned by the federal government. To put this into perspective, in most other parts of the nation that number sits only at 4.2%._ __
[**Browning: With hiring of environmental justice liaisons, state taking another stab at DEI implementation at taxpayer expense**](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[****](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**BY LINDY BROWNING****| COMMENTARY |****DECEMBER 26** _During a time when state legislators are trying to figure out where to cut the budget because of the state operating at what previously was thought to be a $1 billion shortage, the Energy and Carbon Management Commission, previously known as the Colorado Oil and Gas Commission, has announced that they are hiring two new environmental justice liaisons._ __

**🎊 DID YOU KNOW?** The confetti that falls in Times Square at midnight **carries secret messages**. Known as "wishfetti," this tradition began in 2015 and includes thousands of written wishes for the new year. People submit their hopes and dreams either at the Wish Wall in Times Square or online, and these messages are transformed into the colorful confetti that rains down on the crowd to celebrate the start of the year.

We've got to let you know, Team, that a bill that would give President-elect Donald Trump broad powers to target his political foes has passed a major hurdle toward becoming law, recently passing in the U.S. House of Representatives.
The bill, also known as H.R. 9495, would empower the Treasury secretary to unilaterally designate any nonprofit as a “terrorist supporting organization” and revoke its tax-exempt status, effectively killing the group. The bill could give presidential administrations a tool to crack down on organizations for political reasons.
“ Authoritarianism is not born overnight — it creeps in ,” Rep. Lloyd Doggett said on the House floor. “ A tyrant tightens his grip not just by seizing power, but when he demands new powers and when those who can stop him willingly cede and bend to his will .” “ A sixth grader would know this is unconstitutional ,” added Rep. Jamie Raskin.
Unconstitutional and authoritarian or not, this bill has passed the House now and has a good chance of passing both houses of Congress next year. That's why we need to start working now to prevent this bill from ever becoming law.

Hey team, it’s Gretchen. In a minute, I’m going to ask you to pitch in one last donation of the year to Fight Like Hell PAC. But first, let me explain why your gift right now is so important. Just weeks ago, we concluded the November election. I’ve heard the range of emotions folks are feeling, but I want you to know that **the fight didn’t end on November 5th.** In 2023, I launched Fight Like Hell PAC with the mission to elect bold leaders who would put the American people above politics. Our work together helped elect Elissa Slotkin to the United States Senate, Kristen McDonald Rivet to the House of Representatives, and other victories that will help move Michigan forward. That work happens year-round, and we have a lot of exciting plans for 2025 and 2026.
* Hosting in-person trainings for candidates and campaign staff — helping recruit a new generation of leaders and building the Democratic bench from the ground-up.
* Investing early in battleground races — long before they receive national attention.
* Supporting candidates who will defend working people and protect our most fundamental rights.

**All of this work is only possible with you, team. Since launching, folks all across the country have graciously chipped in $10 here or $25 there to power our work — and I couldn’t be more thankful.** [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/99610795/520421075/1155147450?refcode=AU_FLHP_FR_GEN_EOQ_AC90_20241231_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDY0NjIiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiY2I2MmY2MzctYWNjNy1lZjExLTg4Y2UtMDAyMjQ4MmE5M2FmIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=Bv_rMnrL54PYwX5ccui-CftsCT5uaHzAph5AK86d2kg=) Our team is determined to kick off 2025 in the strongest possible position to continue this shared fight, and I’m hoping I can count on your support before the day is over. **[If you’re able, will you pitch in $10 to power Fight Like Hell PAC’s work? clean_body: | Hey team, it’s Gretchen. In a minute, I’m going to ask you to pitch in one last donation of the year to Fight Like Hell PAC. But first, let me explain why your gift right now is so important. Just weeks ago, we concluded the November election. I’ve heard the range of emotions folks are feeling, but I want you to know that the fight didn’t end on November 5th. In 2023, I launched Fight Like Hell PAC with the mission to elect bold leaders who would put the American people above politics. Our work together helped elect Elissa Slotkin to the United States Senate, Kristen McDonald Rivet to the House of Representatives, and other victories that will help move Michigan forward. That work happens year-round, and we have a lot of exciting plans for 2025 and 2026. Hosting in-person trainings for candidates and campaign staff — helping recruit a new generation of leaders and building the Democratic bench from the ground-up. Investing early in battleground races — long before they receive national attention. Supporting candidates who will defend working people and protect our most fundamental rights. All of this work is only possible with you, team. Since launching, folks all across the country have graciously chipped in $10 here or $25 there to power our work — and I couldn’t be more thankful. = Our team is determined to kick off 2025 in the strongest possible position to continue this shared fight, and I’m hoping I can count on your support before the day is over. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | = = | = = | = = I’m ready to fight like hell to defend our fundamental freedoms and for working people. body:
[1]Justice Democrats

Peter,

Tonight at midnight is our final fundraising deadline of the year, so in a
moment, I’m going to ask if you can pitch in. But before I do, I hope
you’ll let me explain just how impactful your contribution will be to
Justice Democrats’ mission.

Political fundraising has slowed down since the November general election
ended, and I can completely understand why. Everyday people are sick and
tired of the Democratic Party claiming to fight for them, only to see them
take massive checks from corporate interests and billionaire donors and
maintain the status quo on their behalf.

Instead of fighting for things working people need and deserve — like
universal healthcare, higher wages, and affordable housing — they continue
to drop billions of dollars on the military-industrial complex and protect
the profits of corporations and the wealthy elite.

It’s enough to dishearten anyone, but we can’t give up and let the powers
that be win. We’re building a movement for bold change in the Democratic
Party led by and for working-class people, and we need you by our side to
be successful.

Justice Democrats is gearing up to launch our 2026 Candidate Recruitment
in the New Year so we can find and support working-class progressives to
challenge out-of-touch Democrats in blue districts all over the country.

That’s why it’s imperative that we reach our $100,000 end-of-year
fundraising goal before the financial quarter comes to a close tonight at
midnight. I’m going to be completely transparent with you: right now,
we’re not on track to hit that amount, but you can change that.

[ https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jd-em-20241231-1?refcode=em20241231-36279&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&refcode2=36279_1203867_uiwOEs&akid=36279%2E1203867%2EuiwOEs ]Please pitch in $5, $50, or whatever you can afford to help reach our
goal and directly fuel Justice Democrats’ work in 2025.

Thank you so much for your support and for being a part of the existential
fight for the soul of the Democratic Party.

In solidarity,

Alexandra Rojas

Peter,

I’m sure you're enjoying the holiday break, so I'll be brief.

Tonight marks my first FEC fundraising deadline as Congressman-elect, and our very first deadline since Election Day.

As you know, Republicans only have a razor-thin majority in Congress. I haven't even been sworn-in yet, and you can bet GOP leadership is already plotting how to make life difficult for incoming, first-year Democrats like me.

Meeting our fundraising goals – especially our first – will set the tone in our broader effort to keep this seat blue. Early strength also helps us navigate this Republican-led Congress so we can make meaningful progress for CA-27.

We set a goal of raising $50,000 before the end of the year. If you can chip in $3, please know that it would go a long way.

Thank you,

George

Without allies and supporters like you, our work to defend our democracy and uphold the rule of law would not be possible. Friend,
Thank you for all that you did in 2024. I know it was a tough election. As I look back on 2024, one thing is abundantly clear: we can’t do this without you. From knocking on doors across the state and donating to talking with your neighbors and heading to the polls, I appreciate all of your hard work. I firmly believe that together we can build a Minnesota that works better for everyone.
These next few years will be challenging, but I’m going to use that as motivation to work even harder. I look forward to working with you in 2025 and beyond.
Happy New Year,
Melissa Hortman
Speaker of the House
Minnesota House of Representatives

| | Friends,

We are less than 12 hours away from the new year! I don't know about you, but I think King County could use some new year's resolutions of its own. Imagine if King County made a new year's resolution to:

* Focus on financial responsibility, instead of compulsively raising taxes every chance it gets
* Fund our law enforcement heroes, instead of disparaging, defunding, and disarming our police
* Prosecute repeat offenders to keep our community safe
* Lower runaway costs of living and make our region more affordable

**_Do you agree with these resolutions? If so, can you rush a donation of_** **_$15, $25 or even $75 before our midnight deadline tonight? [DONATE HERE](https://reagandunn.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=0220f14f6bfeefc23687abe64&id=cf971dc526&e=77eef70c61)!_**

I am running for reelection to the King County Council and am fighting every day for these exact principles. In fact, my personal new year's resolution is to be the last line of defense against extremist Seattle policies that would endanger our communities and cause costs to grow to even more extreme levels.

I am incredibly grateful to have already received the endorsement of all 9 mayors in my district. Would you be willing to join in making a new year's resolution with me to protect our neighborhoods from extreme Seattle policies?

With just 12 hours to go before our midnight deadline, any amount you contribute **before midnight tonight** will send a powerful message to Seattle politicians that we are making a new year's resolution to stand firm against radical Seattle policies.
**_With your help before midnight tonight, we can enter 2025 in a strong position to defend our neighborhoods and communities![ Would you be willing to make a donation right now?](https://reagandunn.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=0220f14f6bfeefc23687abe64&id=3b54cf421e&e=77eef70c61)_**

Reagan Dunn

name: Neil Parrott
subject: Every Action Mattered - Now 2025
body:
Thanks again for your help in 2024. Every action mattered - donating, volunteering, and voting. April & I are so grateful for your help. In November | | | [View this email in your browser](https://us2.campaign-archive.com/?e=5a45ee1154&u=fac7efbc0801875f99034b204&id=9abd201e8c)
---
| |
---
| | Happy New Year's Eve, Peter,

April and I are so grateful for your help. In November, we ended the Congressional race needing additional funds to pay off campaign expenses, and so many people stepped forward to help us.

In the weeks leading up to Christmas, we prayed for help, and we are so thrilled; we have almost paid everything off. Our Christmas was spent giving thanks for all of you and for God's help. I do need to ask you one more time for help. It would be wonderful to finalize everything in the last few hours of 2024. (or the beginning few hours of 2025!)

We have been honored to have you on our "team." This was an intense election cycle. Would you be able to help us one more time with a donation today?

_An immediate donation of_ _ _$15__ __, $50__ __, $200__ __, $500 or even $1000__ _to Parrott for Congress would help us close the account for the new year._
---
| [Donate to Parrott for Congress](https://mdpetitions.us2.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fac7efbc0801875f99034b204&id=07092602ed&e=5a45ee1154 "Donate to Parrott for Congress")
---
| You have been an integral part of our team where we raised and spent over $1.1 Million working to help Republicans take back the House so that we could bring America to a better place for our kids and grandkids. Even though we were very disappointed, for both us and all of our volunteers and supporters, it was a bittersweet night. So many races turned out well.

**April and I want to thank you for all the work you did in 2024**. We made a difference. Thankfully, the Republicans kept the House, took control of the Senate, and now President Trump and his advisors are set to move forward quickly on a positive agenda.

2025 is a New Year where our country needs to secure our southern border, open up our energy supplies, make the tax cuts permanent, and work to stop excessive and unnecessary government spending. It will be exciting to watch.

_Your donation of _$15, $50_ _, $200_ _, $500 or even $1000_ to Parrott for Congress right now will help me close 2024 well and get ready for the next chapter in 2025._
---
| [Donate to Parrott for Congress](https://mdpetitions.us2.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fac7efbc0801875f99034b204&id=27a630ab0b&e=5a45ee1154 "Donate to Parrott for Congress")
---
| **Thanks again for your help in 2024. Every action mattered - donating, volunteering, voting.**

2025 will be here at midnight. As April and I think about goals for our New Year, I know that in some form we will continue to work alongside you to make a positive difference for our families and our country.

Thank you also for considering a donation of _$15, $50_ _, $200_ _, $500 or even $1000_ to Parrott for Congress TONIGHT. I hope to see you in 2025!

For our country and our families,

Neil C. Parrott

[1]Powered By People

Our work has never been about one election, or one candidate.

We’re focused on building the long-term changes to the Texas electorate
that will outlast any one candidate or campaign cycle.

And regardless of what any pundit says, it’s working. Since 2019, we’ve
registered hundreds of thousands Texans to vote — many for the first time.
No neighborhood is too small, too big, too red, or too blue.

And we know Texas will be center stage in the years to come. That’s why
our end-of-year fundraising goal is so critical: $25,000 toward the work
to reach voters in Texas. [ https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20241231.084wVB&refcode=ema20241231-239935&t=1001&akid=239935%2E444211%2ErHjcy6 ]So we’re asking you to invest in that work:
Donate $3 or more right now.

[ https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20241231.084wVB&refcode=ema20241231-239935&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1020&akid=239935%2E444211%2ErHjcy6 ]DONATE $3

We’re in this for the long-haul.

We keep our eyes on the prize, knowing the steps we take today and over
the coming years will allow us to register and mobilize the necessary
voters to ultimately deliver Texas’ 40 electoral college votes to the
Democratic nominee for president for the first time since 1976.

Imagine how much better our country will be then.

Extremists hope we’re too broken, too sad, too defeated to get back off
the mat. We're not, and we know you’re not either — so let’s invest in the
work ahead, together.

[ https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20241231.084wVB&refcode=ema20241231-239935&t=1021&akid=239935%2E444211%2ErHjcy6 ]Help us meet our $25,000 end-of-year fundraising goal: Invest
$3 or more right now.

Thanks — and Happy New Year. We can’t wait to get back to work together.

-Team Powered by People

| December 31, 2024
---
Happy New Year!
Hi Folks! I'd like to start by wishing everyone a happy new year! I realize I’ve been a bit delayed in updating everyone who doesn’t follow us on social media about what’s been happening. **A couple of months ago I accepted a position on the board of directors with the Aurora Resource Center** , formally known as the Thief River Falls Pregnancy Center. The Aurora Resource Center, and other centers like it, are a valuable resource for expectant mothers. Aurora, and other centers like it, lost most of their operating funds last year when the DFL trifecta eliminated the Positive Abortion Alternatives program from the state budget. I hope to collaborate with state legislators, and I’ve already spoken with some who are willing to reintroduce the program in the upcoming legislative session. I’ll include the center’s website at the end of this email. **This past week, I officially closed our state campaign finance account.** I plan to file the paperwork to close the file with the state campaign finance board within the next couple of days. If we do end up running for public office again in the future, we’ll simply start from scratch! Another reason we’ve decided to move forward with this is to have a clean slate as I prepare for the next challenge ahead. **Last month, I submitted an application to compete to be a Regent of the University of Minnesota. **This process is a long and somewhat complex one. The board of regents for the U of M consists of 12 people serving 6-year terms with 4 openings every two years. The board serves as the governing body of the U of M, setting policies, determining goals, and overseeing the budget. They are responsible for the hiring of the President of the University and other important decisions. _If you tend to get bored with details you may wish to skip to the end._ The first step in the process is to submit an application to the Regent Candidate Advisory Council (RCAC). The RCAC is a council appointed by the state legislature to screen potential candidates. I am running for one of two at large positions. It appears there were about 30 applicants, and the RCAC picked 12 to advance to in-person interviews After the first round of voting, I was tied for 5th and invited to the next round. The committee then picks up to 8 candidates to be sent to the legislature for a joint legislative session to select the regents. **So why am I doing this? ******A few reasons... As a graduate of the University of Minnesota Crookston, I felt that the college administration and the board of regents didn’t truly represent or understand the culture of our campus. Requiring COVID vaccines for students to take online classes, while not imposing the same requirements on professors or other university staff felt wrong, as did their reactions to the riots in the cities. But it is much more than that. As you may or may not be aware, the U is a “Land Grant University.” So, what exactly is that? A land grant university is a college or university in the United States that was designated by its state to receive benefits from the Morrill Acts of 1862 and 1890, meaning they were funded by federal land grants and committed to providing practical, accessible education focused on agriculture, mechanics, and military training, aimed at the working class, while also including classical studies. Do you think the University is succeeding in this mission? I do not. Of the 12 regents currently serving, there isn’t one with an agriculture background, and they have no veteran representation. The past two years marked the first time since the board of regents was established that there has been no veteran representation. In addition, we have 5 campuses in the University of Minnesota system yet we have no representation on the regents from the counties or immediate areas of the Crookston or Morris Campuses, rural agricultural areas. To maintain a strong system statewide, we need to have strong individual campuses, including those in greater Minnesota. Each campus should have its own focus area, and that campus should be the primary campus for that area within the greater U of M system. All too often, when we talk about diversity, people are more interested in diversity of appearance over diversity of thought. An article from the university newspaper a couple years ago highlighted the lack of diversity of thought on the board of regents, emphasizing that. From June 2021 to July 2022, the board took 109 votes, 81 of those were unanimous and 28 were split among regents. The majority of those 28 split votes were because 2 regents did not “go with the flow.” One of those regents happened to be the last Veteran to serve as a regent. His name is Darrin Rocha. While running for office has not gone my way the last few elections, **I still want to serve and I still want to make a difference**. So, for now, I am taking a different tack to see if we can make progress from this angle. Thank all of you for your support. We will keep fighting the good fight! My regent interview is scheduled for January 6th. They will announce the final candidates who will be recommended to the legislature on January 10th. I appreciate your well wishes! Have a Happy and Joyous New Year, from my family to yours.

| |

| In Liberty,

Hi Peter — As 2024 comes to a close, I wanted to take some time to reach out and express my appreciation for you. The support you’ve shown me this past year means the world. While we’ve had our fair share of challenges this year, I’m so grateful that folks like you continue to stand with me and support my work of serving Vermonters in Congress. **I also want to acknowledge how tough this election year was.** Donald Trump will return to the White House for his second term in just a few weeks — and Peter, people are scared. They’re hurting. And they’re worried about what the future holds for them and their families. I spoke to a mom recently who came up to me and asked if we could survive four more years of Trump. I hear this concern from Vermonters all the time — and trust me, _I get it._ People have a right to feel that way, but **we cannot let our fear rule us.** That’s why I will continue to approach my work with joy and a clarity of purpose. I have all the confidence in the world that we will navigate through this tough time and continue to make progress for working families. Politics is about making a difference in the lives of regular people — and that work stays the same _regardless_ of who sits in the Oval Office. **I will continue to do everything I can to make Vermont proud. The support you’ve shown me this past year means the world. I also want to acknowledge how tough this election year was. Donald Trump will return to the White House for his second term in just a few weeks — and Peter, people are scared. They’re hurting. And they’re worried about what the future holds for them and their families. I spoke to a mom recently who came up to me and asked if we could survive four more years of Trump. I hear this concern from Vermonters all the time — and trust me, I get it. People have a right to feel that way, but we cannot let our fear rule us. That’s why I will continue to approach my work with joy and a clarity of purpose. I have all the confidence in the world that we will navigate through this tough time and continue to make progress for working families. Politics is about making a difference in the lives of regular people — and that work stays the same regardless of who sits in the Oval Office. Hey Peter, Kevin here, executive director of the Georgia Democratic Party. I don’t normally share our internal memos, but you’re an essential member of our effort to maintain Georgia’s status as a battleground state and build a winning Democratic coalition in 2025, and you need to know these things, too. Here’s the internal update my staff just handed me in our last meeting of the year: | **December 31 — END-OF-YEAR INTERNAL MEMO TOPLINES**
* In 2024, Georgia Democrats increased Kamala Harris's vote total in our state over President Biden’s in 2020 by more than 70,000 votes — more than all other battleground states combined.
* 24 Georgia counties shifted left in 2024 — including several deep red and swing counties.
* Sen. Jon Ossoff is already set to be Republicans’ top target in 2026.

---

body:
What we learned and where we're going in 2025.

| | [ ](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=JgyyvCfQwldlSeD7KJl_Ih7269o_4hwqOhPs1_PHvgI&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=end_of_year_series_volunteer_a&n=1)
---
Tuesday, December 31, 2024 | Peter -- Hey there, I am Carrie Anne, Volunteer Engagement Coordinator for Forward Party. I’ve spent the last 5 years being an activist and volunteering on campaigns, and I’ve taken what I’ve learned by being a volunteer and used that to create the best possible experience for Forward volunteers. **What Went Well** In 2024, the name of the game was candidate support and volunteer activation! Forward rose to the occasion and was able to support 19 candidates across 12 states with text banks. We activated over 50 volunteers to jump in to our slack and CallHub, and offered 10 text banks for them to participate in. A total of over 264,000 texts were sent out! 6 of these text banks supported candidates went on to achieve their goal, with 5 winning and 1 gaining enough vote totals to keep Forward on the ballot for another 4 years in their state. We are now designing a special edition tee shirt for the volunteers who stepped up to the plate to show our appreciation. **Lessons Learned** We did show up to the party a bit late, and missed many voters who had already cast their ballot. We held a volunteer training event, but some who ended up helping us missed it and thus weren't properly trained on things like capturing voter responses. We also would have loved to have been able to support more candidates! [These are our thoughts from 2024, but we want to hear from you! Please head to this link and fill out your thoughts on lessons learned, the direction the party should head in, and projects we should tackle! We will read them all, and we will highlight our top 10, along with the people who submitted them, in early January as our New Years Resolutions.](https://home.forwardparty.com/2024_end_of_year_feedback?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=end_of_year_series_volunteer_a&n=2) **2025 Projects** In 2025 we will get started on all the things earlier. We will offer multiple volunteer trainings, instead of just one, so that people have a better chance of attending. We will use social media more to attract new participants. And we look forward to a streamlined candidate referral and approval process, so we can help more Forward candidates win! Hope this is what you're looking for. Did you get the spreadsheet I shared? It had volunteer responses to the merch distribution form. The function was to collect addresses and sizes, but I put two questions for feedback and there are a few good quotes you could probably use in there about why people volunteer with Forward! I’ve spent the last 5 years being an activist and volunteering on campaigns, and I’ve taken what I’ve learned by being a volunteer and used that to create the best possible experience for Forward volunteers. What Went Well In 2024, the name of the game was candidate support and volunteer activation! Forward rose to the occasion and was able to support 19 candidates across 12 states with text banks. We activated over 50 volunteers to jump in to our slack and CallHub, and offered 10 text banks for them to participate in. A total of over 264,000 texts were sent out! 6 of these text banks supported candidates went on to achieve their goal, with 5 winning and 1 gaining enough vote totals to keep Forward on the ballot for another 4 years in their state. We are now designing a special edition tee shirt for the volunteers who stepped up to the plate to show our appreciation. Lessons Learned We did show up to the party a bit late, and missed many voters who had already cast their ballot. We held a volunteer training event, but some who ended up helping us missed it and thus weren't properly trained on things like capturing voter responses. We also would have loved to have been able to support more candidates! 2025 Projects In 2025 we will get started on all the things earlier. We will offer multiple volunteer trainings, instead of just one, so that people have a better chance of attending. We will use social media more to attract new participants. Dear Peter,

**I was not surprised, but I was disgusted when** the Texas Supreme Court once more failed pregnant Texans earlier this year. ---
Dear Peter,
---
I didn't want to bother you over the Christmas holiday, but I now have something very important to share with you.
---
Reports indicate that my trial is set to begin on January 16 - just days before President Trump's inauguration.
---
**_This trial will determine whether the Left can seize my home in Florida and truly leave me with NOTHING. This is my _final_ chance to save my home._**
---
Since there's no way I can pay the outrageous $148 MILLION judgment against me, they want to rob me of everything I own.
---
They want irreplaceable mementos I gave to my only son. They want personal gifts that I was given by allies abroad to show solidarity with America after the tragedy of September 11th.
---
During these difficult times, Christmas reminded me of what's _truly_ important in life. Earthly possessions come and go - homes, cars, money all come to an end. But the Bible reminds us that _eternal_ "heavenly treasures" await us.
---
The pursuit of truth, freedom, and justice are worth infinitely more than any earthly possession.
---
**I 'd rather lose everything than betray what I know to be true. I could never lie and say what I'm going through is a fair and honest process just to hang on to my possessions.**
---
_"_For what shall it profit a man, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul?_ " (Mark 8:36)_
---

body:
I just wanted to take a moment to personally thank you for all your support this year, Peter. I just wanted to take a moment to personally thank you for all your support this year, Peter.

Together, we fought to keep WA-08 blue – _and we won._

But as always, **our work is far from finished.** Soon, Republicans will control the House, the Senate, and the Oval Office. In 2025, it’s clear that we’ll have our work cut out for us, and we need to do everything we can to hold the line. . .and to hold the GOP and Trump administration accountable when they implement policies that hurt the American People. _That means we simply can’t afford to take our foot off the gas._

So, before you head out for the night, I’m asking for one last push from this team. We need your support to ensure we’re ready to hit the ground running in 2025, and beyond. Can I count on you to chip $5, $10, or any amount you can before the clock strikes midnight? >> [**https://secure.actblue.com/donate/schrier-dec24-personal**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/99629544/520467181/1605543321?refcode=em24_241231_eom4_fndd_gq_act___KSpersonal_ettx&utm_campaign=em24_241231_eom4_fndd_gq_act___KSpersonal_ettx&utm_medium=email&refcode2=06e0a6a4-d2c7-ef11-88ce-0022482a93af&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MTExMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwNmUwYTZhNC1kMmM3LWVmMTEtODhjZS0wMDIyNDgyYTkzYWYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=B7TrIjtrhtY-ohDhlzoQjmrAkcSOksZxyt0PijFLhgM=)
